title: 衣食住行
zh: 旧物店与老屋餐厅，两卷读完。
paragraphs: Morning light fills my small old shop; every piece of [[stuff:stuff]] and every bit of used [[merchandise:merchandise]] holds a past life.
A girl brings a worn travel [[souvenir:souvenir]] and a [[clay:clay]] [[artifact:artifact]] from her kind grandmother.
I check the [[raw:raw]] wood and [[crude:crude]] joints [[first:first]], then plan each [[gentle:gentle]] repair [[step:step]].
Warm coats are a winter [[necessity:necessity]], so today I repair her torn [[festival:festival]] [[outfit:outfit]].
I open my repair [[kit:kit]] and lift each small chrome [[utensil:utensil]] with slow care.
People call these things roadside [[rubbish:rubbish]], but I [[reuse:reuse]] them to make gifts full of warmth.
This bent board came from a [[junk:junk]] pile near the old city [[landfill:landfill]] edge.
After the street [[sewerage:sewerage]] work, [[dust:dust]] covered it, so I washed it with a [[mild:mild]] [[detergent:detergent]].
A caregiver gives me hand [[lotion:lotion]] and a low wide [[tub:tub]] for soaking dirty cloth.
I [[pull:pull]] the small [[plug:plug]] and run the old [[tap:tap]] to rinse the [[frame:frame]] clean.
A short zinc [[pipe:pipe]] and a soft [[hollow:hollow]] [[tube:tube]] hold the legs firmly together.
I clean the floor with a wet [[mop:mop]] and an old [[straw:straw]] [[broom:broom]] before starting work.
An old man brings a thin torn [[mattress:mattress]] and a dusty rolled [[carpet:carpet]].
His small flowered [[rug:rug]] and door [[mat:mat]] need fresh edges and bright new color.
I fill each [[flat:flat]] seat [[cushion:cushion]] with a soft [[feather:feather]] [[pad:pad]] to make it comfortable again.
His baby’s blue [[blanket:blanket]] and the cherished wedding [[quilt:quilt]] both smell of long years in the sun.
A yellowed [[pillow:pillow]] was washed, and its marks were scrubbed out with a soft [[sponge:sponge]].
It was dried with a thick white [[towel:towel]], and its label was clipped on with one small [[staple:staple]].
Each old [[nail:nail]] was pulled out, and the loose edges were cut with a sharp [[razor:razor]].
The [[rough:rough]] corners were [[shave:shaved]] [[smooth:smooth]], and the faulty safety [[fuse:fuse]] was changed.
A black power [[cable:cable]] and a long white [[cord:cord]] dangle behind the desk.
I twirl each loose wire [[strand:strand]], then light a small honey [[candle:candle]].
Warm [[wax:wax]] drips softly while I read repair tips from an old [[paperback:paperback]].
A picture [[pamphlet:pamphlet]] shows old crafts, and I keep small parts in soft [[tissue:tissue]].
I [[xerox:xerox]] the old invoice and put the short [[memorandum:memorandum]] up on the wall above my desk.
My drawer of old [[stationery:stationery]] is messy, but the strong [[glue:glue]] still works well.
Blue [[ink:ink]] marks my notebook while a thick [[rubber:rubber]] [[band:band]] holds the pages.
With a pair of large silver [[scissors:scissors]] I [[shear:shear]] the loose threads from the thick cloth, along the white line.
The [[round:round]] chair [[rim:rim]] is loose, yet each carved [[element:element]] stays truly beautiful.
Cost is one small [[factor:factor]], so I repair only the most damaged [[section:section]].
I shine his old school [[badge:badge]] and tighten each tiny silver [[bolt:bolt]].
A [[round:round]] door [[knob:knob]] and a curved drawer [[handle:handle]] need [[gentle:gentle]] fixing today.
The battered window [[shutter:shutter]] shakes, while the long flowered [[curtain:curtain]] hangs down.
I change the cracked window [[pane:pane]], because its cloudy [[opacity:opacity]] blocks the warm light.
Buttons sleep in a glass [[jar:jar]] and old hooks rest inside a small [[barrel:barrel]].
I carry water in a red [[bucket:bucket]] and rinse my brushes in a small enamel [[pail:pail]].
The shop [[phone:phone]] rings twice, then the little door [[bell:bell]] sings merrily.
My [[portable:portable]] lamp is handy, but the strong [[spotlight:spotlight]] shows every defect.
An old [[paper:paper]] [[lantern:lantern]] glows softly after I change its little warm [[bulb:bulb]].
My pocket [[flashlight:flashlight]] helps me see behind the humming old [[refrigerator:refrigerator]].
The small [[fridge:fridge]] hums while I clean up the [[dust:dust]] with the loud [[vacuum:vacuum]].
A worn delivery [[hurdle:hurdle]] and a fallen garden [[fence:fence]] wait behind the shop.
I oil the loose bike [[pedal:pedal]] and straighten the long leaning wall [[shelf:shelf]].
I [[climb:climb]] my short red [[ladder:ladder]] to reach the high three-legged [[painting:painting]] [[stool:stool]] in the corner.
A torn black [[umbrella:umbrella]] and a yellowed child's [[raincoat:raincoat]] [[drip:drip]] by the door.
I [[dredge:dredge]] the thick mud from the bottom of the old well, then [[pour:pour]] it into a rusty enamel [[can:can]].
The old [[mill:mill]] has closed down, so I warm the joints at a neighbor’s small [[forge:forge]].
This light [[alloy:alloy]] [[frame:frame]] is softer than pure [[metal:metal]].
An old [[flat:flat]] [[iron:iron]] stands beside a shining candlestick of yellow [[brass:brass]].
A small green [[bronze:bronze]] [[horse:horse]] and a bag of grey [[cement:cement]] sit together.
White powdered [[lime:lime]] and [[smooth:smooth]] wall [[plaster:plaster]] repair the cracked corner nicely.
A cracked brown [[leather:leather]] bag and a clear [[plastic:plastic]] cover wait for care.
Each plant [[fibre:fibre]] feels [[rough:rough]], while the soft blue [[fabric:fabric]] feels [[smooth:smooth]].
Grandma loves to [[knit:knit]] warm caps, and I [[weave:weave]] the torn seat again.
A thick painted [[canvas:canvas]] and white table [[linen:linen]] cover the worktop.
Soft white [[cotton:cotton]] shirts and a strong blue [[nylon:nylon]] bag hang outdoors to dry.
Freshly cut [[lumber:lumber]] smells sweet, and each [[wooden:wooden]] leg shines after oiling.
A date [[pit:pit]] lies near the heater, where wood is our [[steady:steady]] winter [[fuel:fuel]].
I [[lubricate:lubricate]] each stiff hinge, then suspend a clear shining [[crystal:crystal]] pendant.
No [[inferior:inferior]] parts stay here, and every [[counterfeit:counterfeit]] coin goes back to the man who brought it.
A [[fake:fake]] pearl breaks fast, for its thin painted shell is quite [[fragile:fragile]].
A [[miniature:miniature]] chair model is the only gift still [[available:available]] today.
Strong seams make each repair [[durable:durable]], and that slowly wins me [[popularity:popularity]] with the neighbors.
Short capes are in [[vogue:vogue]], but warm snugness will always [[prevail:prevail]] here.
A young [[idol:idol]] loves [[plain:plain]] dress, not the flashy [[luxury:luxury]] of the shops.
No [[extravagant:extravagant]] spending is needed when old family [[jewellery:jewellery]] shines anew.
Each tiny bright [[jewel:jewel]] and polished blue [[gem:gem]] glow in the little dish on my table.
A pale green [[jade:jade]] ring will [[adorn:adorn]] the old music box cover.
Every small gold [[ornament:ornament]] will [[embellish:embellish]] the [[plain:plain]] [[festival:festival]] dress.
I [[embroider:embroider]] red flowers while my sister practises [[gentle:gentle]] wedding [[hairdressing:hairdressing]] on a young bride.
[[natural:Natural]] green [[pigment:pigment]] and a safe brown [[dye:dye]] color the pale cloth.
For the [[spring:spring]] [[masquerade:masquerade]] dance, she wears a thin shining [[veil:veil]].
Her old dance [[costume:costume]] will [[fascinate:fascinate]] every child in front.
A [[decent:decent]] clean hem looks good, and neat buttons add an [[exquisite:exquisite]] touch.
She walks with [[gentle:gentle]] [[grace:grace]] and [[quiet:quiet]] simple [[elegance:elegance]] each day.
Her neat new [[appearance:appearance]] needs no costly shop [[cosmetics:cosmetics]] at all.
Light soft [[makeup:makeup]] keeps her looking sweet and [[charming:charming]] through the day.
We [[clothe:clothe]] the child warmly and repair each torn school [[garment:garment]].
The freshly folded [[laundry:laundry]] fills the small [[wardrobe:wardrobe]] in her tidied bedroom again.
His work [[overall:overalls]] are so dusty that he borrows a long grey [[overcoat:overcoat]].
A soft morning [[robe:robe]] and a long evening [[gown:gown]] hang behind the screen.
I repair a blue winter [[sweater:sweater]] and a brown biking [[jacket:jacket]].
His grey work [[trousers:trousers]] need a strong button and a small silver [[clasp:clasp]].
I shape the bent hat [[brim:brim]] and wash a soft flowered [[scarf:scarf]].
A white dotted [[handkerchief:handkerchief]] and a small buttoned [[purse:purse]] lie together.
I keep a worn brown [[wallet:wallet]] and a grey sleeveless [[vest:vest]].
I [[wrap:wrap]] the gift neatly and hang her dark theatre [[cloak:cloak]] inside the cupboard.
The white shirt [[collar:collar]] is bent, and one [[sleeve:sleeve]] of the long coat is too short.
One warm winter [[sock:sock]] and a thin party [[stocking:stocking]] are still waiting for their matching pairs.
Her pink soft [[slipper:slippers]] are worn through, but the white [[lace:lace]] edging still looks pretty.
The kind old [[tailor:tailor]] will [[sew:sew]] the hem before the evening show.
We [[spin:spin]] the yarn smoothly and add one strong hidden [[stitch:stitch]].
My sharp chrome [[needle:needle]] flashes, and each colored [[pin:pin]] holds the pleat.
A long red [[string:string]] and a thin white [[thread:thread]] lie beside the roller.
A torn bag [[strap:strap]] hangs loose, while a painted wall [[stripe:stripe]] guides my cut.
A pink satin [[ribbon:ribbon]] ties the box, and a black school [[belt:belt]] needs holes.
A thin gold [[chain:chain]] shines beside her small new [[bracelet:bracelet]].
Her old pearl [[necklace:necklace]] broke, so I renew its silk and every tiny fallen [[bead:bead]].
The [[textile:textile]] scraps I saved and a piece of red [[velvet:velvet]] fill the box.
Soft grey [[wool:wool]] and a flowered knee [[patch:patch]] save the old coat.
I wipe the worktop with a torn cleaning [[rag:rag]], here in our [[shabby:shabby]] but cozy corner.
The [[tight:tight]] [[belt:belt]] is eased, and a calm deep [[purple:purple]] shade hides the repair.
A soft [[tan:tan]] coat is cleaned so its warm color will never [[fade:fade]].
Each dark food [[stain:stain]] and each paint [[blot:blot]] slowly fades from the cloth.
The tall singer is quite a [[figure:figure]] on our street today, and she looks [[slender:slender]] in the fixed dress.
At [[dusk:dusk]] we share tea, thankful for each [[slight:slight]] repair that warms our street.
Grandma announced the plan for the [[erection:erection]] of a new hall, ignoring every past [[stricture:stricture]] about money.
Mom agreed to [[construct:construct]] a warm dining hall, though old [[dust:dust]] could [[obstruct:obstruct]] or [[ruin:ruin]] dinner.
Mingming wanted to [[establish:establish]] clear duties, starting with washing the gray [[concrete:concrete]] floor.
Uncle Wang brought bright [[steel:steel]] tools, ensuring strength and long [[stability:stability]] for shelves.
They walked around the dusty [[site:site]], dreaming about how the future [[venue:venue]] would welcome guests.
The old house was a village [[landmark:landmark]], quietly [[situated:situated]] beside green trees and [[narrow:narrow]] paths.
Mom tried to [[locate:locate]] the old drawings in the corner where grandpa once chose to [[reside:reside]] and cook.
Small birds still [[inhabit:inhabit]] the roof, but they will [[migrate:migrate]] elsewhere after the noise begins.
Grandma decided to [[settle:settle]] downstairs, keeping the whole [[dwelling:dwelling]] [[lively:lively]] day and [[night:night]].
Mingming joked that their home was no [[skyscraper:skyscraper]] and no rich [[villa:villa]], yet it was full of love.
Unlike a cold [[mansion:mansion]] or crowded [[apartment:apartment]], this place kept childhood memories alive.
They refused to make it into a noisy [[hostel:hostel]] or hunting [[lodge:lodge]] for strangers.
Behind the yard stood a weak [[hut:hut]] and a [[wooden:wooden]] [[cabin:cabin]] full of battered chairs.
Mom opened the dark [[cellar:cellar]] and the leaning [[shed:shed]], coughing through thick [[dust:dust]].
The small [[cottage:cottage]] next door once served as a daytime [[nursery:nursery]] for village kids.
Mingming found his tiny [[cradle:cradle]] there, now a safe [[shelter:shelter]] for kittens.
Uncle Wang moved each fallen [[block:block]], then drew a neat [[grid:grid]] on [[paper:paper]] for the cleaning plan.
They swept a [[narrow:narrow]] [[aisle:aisle]] [[first:first]], then cleared leaves across the wide [[porch:porch]].
[[dust:Dust]] covered the long [[corridor:corridor]], while [[spider:spider]] webs hung along the shaky [[staircase:staircase]].
The upper [[storey:storey]] held a thick [[layer:layer]] of [[ash:ash]] that made everyone sneeze loudly.
Mingming joked that this old house had no [[escalator:escalator]], gripping the loose [[wooden:wooden]] [[handrail:handrail]] tightly.
Grandma wiped one stone [[pillar:pillar]] after another, counting each tall [[column:column]] aloud.
A cracked [[wooden:wooden]] [[beam:beam]] held up the curved [[vault:vault]] above the main hall.
Mom praised the [[round:round]] [[arch:arch]] and the high [[ceiling:ceiling]] that kept summer air cool.
Sparrows nested under wide [[eaves:eaves]], near the tall stone [[chimney:chimney]] full of soot.
They planned a simple [[reception:reception]] corner, brighter than any hotel [[lobby:lobby]] in town.
With the rickety [[wooden:wooden]] [[bench:bench]] gone, the old [[parlour:parlour]] looked empty and sad.
Grandma kept the stone [[fireplace:fireplace]] but removed the rusty [[iron:iron]] [[radiator:radiator]] beside it.
Mingming cleaned the dusty [[living room:living room]] shelves, polishing every [[wooden:wooden]] [[cabinet:cabinet]] door.
Mom opened the sunny [[balcony:balcony]] doors, sweeping dry leaves off the stone [[terrace:terrace]].
The old [[kitchen:kitchen]] smelled of smoke, worse than the forgotten back [[lavatory:lavatory]] nearby.
Uncle Wang scrubbed the yellowed [[toilet:toilet]] seat, then wiped the edge of the stained [[bath:bath]] [[tub:tub]].
Unlike the noisy town [[mall:mall]] or stone shopping [[complex:complex]], home felt calm.
They listed needed items, skipping the distant [[supermarket:supermarket]] and [[night:night]] market [[booth:booth]].
Nobody wanted a flashy [[casino:casino]] or noisy photo [[studio:studio]]; they wanted warm meals.
Though the town grew and felt more [[urban:urban]] every year, their own alley stayed [[quiet:quiet]], almost [[peripheral:peripheral]], like a dream.
Shops in the near [[vicinity:vicinity]] closed early, leaving the [[night:night]] street an empty [[void:void]].
After we cleared the [[junk:junk]], the hall looked [[spacious:spacious]] yet dusty, far from [[airtight:airtight]] and safe.
Mingming ran across the wide [[expanse:expanse]] toward the small front [[plaza:plaza]], shouting with pleasure.
He imagined the house as a storybook [[castle:castle]], then watched the old [[carpenter:carpenter]] appear.
The careful [[mason:mason]] tapped each loose floor [[tile:tile]], humming an old village [[tune:tune]].
By [[sunset:sunset]], fresh gray [[brickwork:brickwork]] along the doorway promised many busy mornings ahead.
Mingming woke with a sharp [[appetite:appetite]], impatient to help Mom [[cater:cater]] for tomorrow’s guests.
They checked the food they had stored, keeping only fresh [[edible:edible]] things as a [[provision:provision]] for the week.
Grandma shared a secret [[recipe:recipe]], planning to make the old hall into a small [[restaurant:restaurant]].
Unlike the school [[refectory:refectory]] or the noisy street [[bar:bar]], the food at home would be [[gentle:gentle]] and warm.
They refused the dull [[cafeteria:cafeteria]] lines and the costly hotel [[buffet:buffet]] for the big dinner in the hall.
Uncle Wang offered his yard [[barbecue:barbecue]] stand, freeing the family [[supper:supper]] from dull routines.
Grandma dreamed of a [[harvest:harvest]] [[banquet:banquet]], with warm tea as [[refreshment:refreshment]] for every child.

Mom praised village [[cuisine:cuisine]], refusing greasy street [[takeaway:takeaway]] boxes that [[night:night]].

They also cooked for a [[vegetarian:vegetarian]] aunt, borrowing clean extra [[cutlery:cutlery]] from neighbors.

Grandma lifted white [[porcelain:porcelain]] plates, placing a small flower [[saucer:saucer]] beneath each cup.
Mingming carried a [[wooden:wooden]] [[tray:tray]] and a [[mug:mug]] of warm milk without spilling a bit.

Uncle Wang hid his [[whisky:whisky]] bottle and his sweet [[brandy:brandy]] from the kids.
Nobody arrived [[drunk:drunk]] for dinner, though old [[tobacco:tobacco]] smell lingered in coats.
Grandma threw away a wet [[cigarette:cigarette]] end, keeping her head clear and [[sober:sober]].
At [[dawn:dawn]] they picked green [[pea:pea]] pods and crisp long [[cucumber:cucumbers]] in the garden.
Mom chose [[round:round]] [[cabbage:cabbage]] heads and shiny [[purple:purple]] [[eggplant:eggplants]] for stew.
Mingming pulled orange [[carrot:carrot]] roots and [[flat:flat]] white [[turnip:turnip]] heads from soft soil.

Mingming traded two bunches of [[purple:purple]] [[grape:grapes]] for two soft, sweet [[papaya:papayas]].
Grandma dried red [[plum:plum]] slices, thanking the autumn [[crop:crop]] for lavish gifts.
Uncle Wang carried golden ears of [[corn:corn]] and heavy [[grain:grain]] sacks into the yard.

Mom mixed white [[flour:flour]] with water, cooking thick morning [[porridge:porridge]] for all.
Mingming stirred the sticky rice [[paste:paste]], watching the village [[livestock:livestock]] come up to the fences.
They chose a fat village [[chicken:chicken]] and a stately brown [[turkey:turkey]] for the [[feast:feast]].

Grandma seasoned dark [[mutton:mutton]] chunks, adding a long smoked [[sausage:sausage]] for flavor.
Uncle Wang netted a silver [[fish:fish]] from the clear [[pond:pond]] behind the bamboo grove.
He carved a new fishing [[rod:rod]], trading fresh milk and [[dairy:dairy]] food with the neighbors.
Mingming tasted thick white [[yogurt:yogurt]] and spread soft yellow [[butter:butter]] on bread.
They shared a warm [[hamburger:hamburger]] and a crusty [[loaf:loaf]] of brown bread at noon.
Mom baked a [[round:round]] apple [[pie:pie]] and boiled thin long [[pasta:pasta]] for the kids.
Grandma twirled the long [[spaghetti:spaghetti]] into nests, chilling sweet milk [[pudding:pudding]] for dessert.
Mingming crunched a square [[biscuit:biscuit]] and spread red strawberry [[jam:jam]] thick on his bread.

Mom passed the strong yellow [[mustard:mustard]] and a tiny dab of green [[wasabi:wasabi]] carefully.
Uncle Wang crushed the black [[pepper:pepper]] grains, slicing pale yellow [[ginger:ginger]] [[root:root]] thinly.
Mingming minced white [[garlic:garlic]] cloves and the long green [[scallion:scallions]] for the soup.
They sprinkled a few drops of clear rice [[vinegar:vinegar]] and added a small pinch of white [[salt:salt]].
Grandma loved the [[mild:mild]] [[fruit:fruit]] [[flavour:flavour]], not the sharp [[sour:sour]] taste from unripe plums.
Mingming spat out the [[bitter:bitter]] skin, reaching instead for the warm soup, [[mild:mild]] and [[spicy:spicy]].
The guests called the stew [[delicious:delicious]] and said the warm buns were simply [[yummy:yummy]].
The hot noodles were [[tasty:tasty]], perfect for [[thirsty:thirsty]] workers after a long day.
Mom ground red [[spice:spice]] powder, simmering thick tomato [[sauce:sauce]] slowly.
Mingming squeezed red [[ketchup:ketchup]] lines, while roses gave [[natural:natural]] [[perfume:perfume]] nearby.

Uncle Wang helped [[fry:fry]] golden potato shreds, then watched grandma [[roast:roast]] chestnuts slowly.
They served crisp morning [[toast:toast]], warning the kids not to [[suck:suck]] the hot soup too fast.
Mingming learned to [[swallow:swallow]] his food calmly, refusing to [[lick:lick]] his fingers at the table.

Mom told him to [[soak:soak]] dry mushrooms, then briefly [[dip:dip]] greens in boiling water.
Grandma taught Mingming to [[squeeze:squeeze]] oranges and gently [[stir:stir]] honey into tea.
At last mom began to [[grind:grind]] sesame seeds, filling the yard with nutty fragrance.
They hung the [[paper:paper]] lamps with thin [[suspension:suspension]] cords, tying each [[knot:knot]] on an [[iron:iron]] [[hook:hook]].
Mingming pulled the [[wooden:wooden]] [[lever:lever]], steadying the tall bamboo [[scaffold:scaffold]] for uncle.

Grandma asked uncle to [[fix:fix]] the wires and carefully [[mend:mend]] the torn tablecloths till morning.

Uncle Wang began to [[weld:weld]] chair legs, while Mingming held the sharp [[saw:saw]] [[steady:steady]].

Grandma tested the well wall with a straight [[plumb:plumb]] line before fetching clear water, dreaming of a stone [[viaduct:viaduct]] in her hometown.
They used a model of a small earth [[dam:dam]], learning how workers [[assemble:assemble]] bridges together.
Workers came to [[install:install]] bright lamps and [[furnish:furnish]] corners with flowers and stools.
Mingming admired the neat [[placement:placement]] of bowls and the [[clever:clever]] table [[layout:layout]].

Grandma led the tours through the [[inner:inner]] rooms, showing the renewed [[interior:interior]] with pride.

sentZh: 晨光洒满我的小店：每一件旧物、每一件二手商品，都藏着一段过去。
女孩带来一件旅行时买的旧纪念品，还有奶奶传下的泥塑工艺品。
我先检查未加工的木料和粗糙的接头，再定下每一步轻巧的修补计划。
暖和的外套是冬天的必需品，所以我今天先补好她那件撕破的节日盛装。
我打开修补工具箱，慢慢拿起每一件小小的镀铬用具。
人们叫这些东西路边垃圾，可我把它们重新利用，做成暖暖的礼物。
这块弯木板来自旧城垃圾填埋场边上的废品堆。
街道排污施工以后，它落满了灰，所以我用温和的洗涤剂把它洗了一遍。
护理员送我护手乳和一只矮宽盆，用来泡脏布。
我拔掉小塞子，打开旧水龙头，把架子冲干净。
一截短锌管和一根软空心管，把腿牢牢固定在一起。
开工前我先用湿拖把和旧草扫帚拖地扫地。
老人带来一张又薄又破的床垫和一卷落灰的地毯。
他的小碎花地毯和门口垫子要包新边，添新色。
我在每个瘪了的坐垫里塞进柔软的羽毛垫芯，让它重新坐得舒服。
